# claude.md - Register Errands - VI Dynamic (tree 756760393)

## Purpose
ETG (eTraveli Group) SUBTREE of "Register Errands - Dynamic" (tree 595124299), for the
Self Transfer Guarantee / Virtual Interlining (VI) contact reasons. It collects the VI
eligibility + disruption details, the STG offer the agent made, the passengers on the
combined itinerary, the Edvin type and the customer action, and hands ONE combined-PNR
errand record back to the parent tree, which owns all Zendesk ticket creation, the
internal note and the Edvin registration.

Entered from the parent tree's node 76 (Tree node, open_tree_id 756760393,
open_tree_node_id 0 -> this tree's root, return_tree_node_id 3). The parent reaches it from
its node 75 "Is VI Selection", which matches custom_field_29658558478738 against
contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi,
contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi_sc and
contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi_passengers_at_the_airport.
This tree exits at node 79 (Tree node, "Return Parent", open_tree_id 1 = return to the
calling tree); the parent resumes at its node 3 (any child tickets?) -> child/silent
ticket loop -> 21 internal note -> 22 -> 44 Edvin registration loop. (VI never produces a
grandchild ticket - see Conventions & gotchas.)

## Architecture (flow)
```
83 Set VI Combined PNR   (ROOT - collapses the selected PNRs into one record, resets VI state)
  -> 82 Partner / order-age route    (sets form data `route`; reads `partner`/`orderCreated`
                                       as inbound values - no agent-facing screen sets them
                                       in this tree, see Open items #6)
  -> 85 Select Passengers - VI       (agent picks passengers via the findorder Dynamic View)
  -> 86 Continue                     (attaches passengers/formatted_passengers to current_pnr)
  -> 49 Partner logic                (route == "50" -> 50, else -> 66)
       50 Bcom OR ETG & prior 21May26      66 ETG & post 22may2026
       [dropdowns: disruption_type, delay_reason (Trip delay), flight_affected (Schedule*)]
  -> 52 (from 50) / 67 (from 66) route on disruption + flight:
       Schedule change (within/outside 24h) -> 53 (Booking) / 69 (ETG)
       Trip delay                           -> 62 (Booking) / 73 (ETG)
       Accomodation / Meal compensation     -> 80
  STG offer ladder - each screen exits to 80 when an offer is taken, or falls to the next:
       Booking: 53 -> 58 -> {80 | 59} ; 59 -> 60 -> {80 | 61} ; 61 -> 80
                62 -> 63 -> {80 | 64} ; 64 -> 65 -> {80 | 61}
       ETG:     69 -> 70 -> {80 | 71} ; 71 -> 72 -> {80 | 61}
                73 -> 74 -> {80 | 75} ; 75 -> 76 -> {80 | 61}
  -> 80 Get Errand Configurations  (Data node, CO 182 + 183)
  -> 81 Format Types               (channel/category + types_list/actions_by_type/...)
  -> 1  Agent - Select Channel & Type  [select: type (dynamic from category.types), notes]
  -> 2  Dynamic Actions List Options   (actions_array, VI details, records the combined PNR)
  -> 12 Create PNR Action Table -> 25 Display PNR Action Table  (agent picks the action)
  -> 27 Stitch & Group  -> 84 Set VI Finals (combined PNR) -> 79 Return Parent
```
Node 5 is this claude.md - unlinked, never in the flow.

## Data dictionary
- transforms.selected_pnrs: the order-grid rows the agent picked, set by the PARENT tree's
  node 24 from views.findorder. INPUT to this tree.
- transforms.current_pnr: THE COMBINED PNR record. Built by node 83 from selected_pnrs
  (pnr = every selected PNR joined with ", "), given `passengers`/`formatted_passengers` by
  node 86, enriched by node 2 (channel, category, type, notes, vi_details, actions_array),
  resolved by node 27 (customer_action, bucket, bucketId, actionId), and republished by
  node 84 as the final record.
- transforms.combined_pnr_record / transforms.combined_pnr: the node 83 baseline record and
  the joined PNR string. combined_pnr is mirrored as form data.
- passengers / formatted_passengers (on current_pnr and every downstream record derived
  from it): set by node 86 from views.findorder after the agent picks passengers on node 85.
  `passengers` is the raw array ({passengerFirstName, passengerLastName, passengerType,
  passengerId, ...}); `formatted_passengers` is the HTML block node 12's preview card and
  node 25 render. Both fields are plain object properties, so they ride through every
  `...spread` in nodes 2, 27 and 84 unchanged with no per-node wiring - node 27 is the only
  place that explicitly re-touches them (mergePassengers, for the child_ticket and note).
- transforms.channel / transforms.category: Edvin channel + category OBJECTS, resolved by
  node 81 from actions.edvin__errand_configuration and actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value.
  This tree fetches its own config at node 80 - it no longer depends on the parent's node 46.
- transforms.types_list / types_by_id / actions_by_type / actions_by_type_name /
  actions_flat: node 81's groupings. actions_by_type["<typeId>"] is what node 2 reads, and
  category.types is the dynamic list source behind node 1's `type` select.
- transforms.actions_array: the normalized actions for the selected type, taken from
  actions_by_type. Item shape {id, name, bucket (STRING routing key), bucketId, actionId,
  edvin_actions, type_id, type_name}.
- transforms.customer_action_pnrs: the customer-action rows the table on nodes 12/25
  renders. On the VI path this holds exactly ONE row - the combined PNR. Upserted by pnr in
  node 2, restitched in node 27, replaced with the final record in node 84. The parent's
  node 21 prints the internal note from this list (including `**Passengers**` per record,
  from `record.passengers`).
- transforms.vi_details / transforms.vi_details_text: the VI/STG answers as an object and as
  printable text. Captured in node 2, stored on the record, and folded into the record's
  `notes` so the parent prints them in the internal note (its node 21, "Notes") and in the
  Edvin errand free text (its node 44, "Agent Notes") with no parent-side change.
- transforms.child_tickets: [{child_ticket:{... passengers, formatted_passengers,
  grandchild_tickets: []}}]. Built by node 27 directly from the one stitched row - NOT
  grouped by (type+customer_action), because there is only ever one row (see Conventions &
  gotchas, "ONE COMBINED PNR, NEVER GRANDCHILDREN"). `grandchild_tickets` is always `[]`;
  kept only so the parent's node 32 loop (which reads `current_child_ticket.grandchild_tickets
  || []`) sees the shape it expects. Consumed by the parent's node 32 loop, whose ticket body
  reads `payload.passengers` for the Passengers section.
- transforms.final_pnrs: THE hand-off. Exactly ONE entry on the VI path (the combined PNR,
  including `passengers`/`formatted_passengers`), written by node 84. The parent's node 44
  registers one Edvin errand per entry and reads `rec.passengers` for the errand's
  "Passengers" line.
- transforms.unresolved_selections + has_unresolved_selections /
  unresolved_selections_count (form data): node 27 diagnostics for a customer action it
  could not resolve to an (action, known bucket) pair. Recorded and logged only - this tree
  has no re-pick screen yet. See Open items.
- Form-data scalars published by node 84 for logic nodes and Connected Objects:
  combined_pnr, customer_action, customer_action_id, bucket, bucket_id, errand_type,
  stg_outcome, stg_trail. `type` is deliberately NOT overwritten - it holds the Edvin type ID that node
  1's select and node 2's lookup depend on.
- Record fields that follow the v5 hand-off contract (node 118 of
  "Register Errands - VI Dynamic (v5 subtree-only 2026-08-20).json") so the two designs stay
  interchangeable: pnr (joined), postSaleHandleType / providerSystem (joined with " / "),
  id + providerPnrIds (FLAT array of provider booking ids), vi_pnr_count, and the flattened
  partner / disruption_type / delay_reason / flight_affected / stg_outcome. Node 84 also
  builds providerBookingIds itself, as JSON.stringify of the FLAT, de-duped id array - the
  parent's node 27 builds it as JSON.stringify(group.map(i => i.id)), which nests on a
  collapsed record because `id` is already an array. It reads the FIRST source that has ids
  (providerPnrIds, then id, then the node 83 baseline), never a concatenation of all three -
  they all hold the same ids, so concatenating triples the list.
- transforms.isMorePNR is set false by nodes 83 and 84, so the collapsed record can never be
  routed into the parent's per-PNR loop (its node 11) whichever node the parent returns
  through.
- route / order_created_date (form data): node 82's routing scalar and the date it resolved.
- stg_outcome / stg_trail (form data + record fields, node 84): the STG ladder is walked
  top-down and every rung the agent could not fill answers "None of the above is available",
  so the OUTCOME is the LAST rung that named a real offer - not the first answer found. All
  declines means the outcome genuinely is "None of the above is available". stg_trail keeps
  every answer in ladder order, joined with " -> ", for the note.
- VI selection variables (form data, cleared by node 83 on entry): partner, orderCreated,
  route, disruption_type, delay_reason, flight_affected, stg_alternatives_sameday_sc,
  stg_alternatives_overnight_sc, stg_alternatives_sameday_td, stg_alternatives_overnight_td,
  stg_refund.

## External systems (CX Actions / Connected Objects)
- Node 80 "Get Errand Configurations" - Data node, org 116, CO **182** and **183**, producing
  actions.edvin__errand_configuration and actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value.
- Node 85 "Select Passengers - VI" - Dynamic View (dcoId 23, alias `findorder`, widgetId 55,
  grid). Agent-facing selection only; node 86 reads the pick back via `views.findorder`.
- Nothing else in this tree calls an API. Every Zendesk and Edvin WRITE happens in the
  parent tree after node 79 returns.

## Conventions & gotchas
- ONE COMBINED PNR, ONE ERRAND. VI is a self-transfer itinerary: the PNRs are legs of the
  same journey, so they collapse into a single record (node 83) and produce a single Edvin
  errand and a single child/silent ticket. Do not reintroduce the parent tree's per-PNR loop
  (its nodes 7/11) here.
- ONE COMBINED PNR, NEVER GRANDCHILDREN (confirmed 2026-08-24). Because node 2 upserts by
  pnr and the VI path only ever has the one combined pnr, transforms.customer_action_pnrs
  never holds more than one row by the time node 27 runs. Grandchild tickets only exist
  when 2+ DISTINCT (type+customer_action) rows share one PROCEED bucket - impossible with
  one row. Node 27 no longer contains the parent's (type+action) grouping / grandchild-
  building code; it builds the single ticket directly from row 0 and logs a warning (rather
  than silently dropping data) if more than one row ever reaches it. `grandchild_tickets` is
  still published as `[]` on the child_ticket object for shape-compatibility with the
  parent's node 32 loop - it is just never populated. Do NOT port this simplification to the
  parent tree's own node 27 - it genuinely handles multiple PNRs and multiple actions per
  run and still needs the grouping/grandchild logic.
- ONE PRODUCER OF BUCKET KEYS. Edvin returns bucket as {id, name} where `name` is a HUMAN
  LABEL ("No action", "Proceed", "Different request"), not the snake_case key this workflow
  routes on. Node 81 maps it ID-first (BUCKET_BY_ID {3: no_action, 4: proceed,
  5: different_request}), name map as fallback, unmapped returned UNCHANGED and never
  guessed. **Node 2 reads node 81's actions_by_type rather than re-mapping** - it used to
  keep its own label-only copy, which is exactly why every bucket except "Proceed" reached
  node 27 unusable. Node 2 still carries the same block as a fallback for a session where
  node 81 has not run; if you ever edit one, edit both.
- ACTION RESOLUTION IS ID-OR-NAME. Node 12 currently renders action NAMES as its option
  values; node 27 matches actionId, then id, then name, so either render resolves. If node
  12 is ever hardened to emit action IDs (the parent tree's v29 build), node 27 needs no
  change.
- PASSENGERS ARE CAPTURED ONCE, ON NODE 85/86, THEN JUST RIDE ALONG. Node 86 is the only
  place `passengers`/`formatted_passengers` are computed from `views.findorder`; every node
  after it (2, 27, 84) only ever spreads the record forward, never re-derives them. If a
  future edit rebuilds `current_pnr` or a stitched row from scratch instead of spreading the
  previous value, it will silently drop passengers - always spread the incoming record first,
  then override specific keys.
- READ TRANSFORMS AS `transforms.<name>`, NEVER `ZT.getVariableValue(...)` - THAT READS
  FORM DATA. **Fixed 2026-08-24**: node 86 used to read the node-83 record with
  `ZT.getVariableValue("combined_pnr_record")`. That namespace only holds form-data scalars
  (query params, form fields) - the record was written with `ZT.setTransformData`, which
  lives in the separate `transforms` namespace and must be read back as
  `transforms.combined_pnr_record`. The old code silently got back "" instead of throwing,
  so `{...combined_pnr_record, passengers, formatted_passengers}` collapsed to JUST
  `{passengers, formatted_passengers}` - erasing `pnr` (and everything else node 83 built)
  for the rest of the tree. That is what was producing "Child Ticket: undefined" /
  "Silent Ticket: undefined" ticket titles out of node 27 - row.pnr was undefined by the
  time node 27 built the title. Node 86 now reads `transforms.combined_pnr_record ||
  transforms.current_pnr || {}`, matching the parent tree's own node 9 ("Format
  Passengers"), which never had this bug. Any future script in this tree that needs to
  read back a value set with `ZT.setTransformData` must use `transforms.<name>` - never
  `ZT.getVariableValue`, which is for the form-data/default namespace only.
- keep_vars_on_back = 1. It was 0, so any Back navigation through the VI screens discarded
  the captured values - an independent way to lose the customer action and its bucket. The
  parent tree hit the same thing and fixed it the same way (its v26).
- Node 83 clears the VI selection variables on entry because form data never expires. A
  second contact in the same session would otherwise inherit the previous disruption/STG
  answers, and a conditional field that is no longer shown would still post its old value.
- THE CUTOFF COMPARE IS DATE-ONLY AND TIMEZONE-FREE (node 82). `new Date('2026-05-21T00:00:00')`
  parses as LOCAL midnight while Edvin's orderCreated is an ISO timestamp, so a late-20-May
  order could fall either side depending on where the engine runs. Node 82 compares
  YYYY-MM-DD prefixes as strings instead. It prefers the agent-entered `orderCreated`
  variable, then the API value, and logs a warning when neither is readable (route then
  falls back to "66"). There is no agent-facing screen in this tree that sets `partner` or
  `orderCreated` any more (see Open items #6) - they arrive as inbound values already set
  before this tree is reached. BOUNDARY: an order created ON 2026-05-21 routes to node 66 -
  unchanged from the original, but node 50 is titled "prior 21May26" and 66
  "post 22may2026", so the 21st itself is not described by either. Confirm with ETG.
- THE STG OPTION STRINGS ARE THE CONTRACT. Every alternatives screen is followed by a logic
  node comparing the selected value to the exact option text, so an edited option label must
  be edited in BOTH places. Trailing spaces are silent killers: node 71's first option used
  to end in a space and node 72's expression did not, so that branch fell through to its
  default (button_link 0, a dead end).
- Selections are DROPDOWNS (native `select` formfields), not radios, as of 2026-08-21 (v7).
  Each keeps its original variable name so every logic expression still matches. Static
  option lists with {"filterable":true}.
- Selections are DROPDOWNS (native `select` formfields), not radios, as of 2026-08-21 (v7).
  Each keeps its original variable name so every logic expression still matches. Static
  option lists with {"filterable":true}.
- DROPDOWNS ARE REQUIRED, NOT PLACEHOLDER-LED, AS OF 2026-08-24 (Brent's dropdown edit,
  merged this session). The "- Select -" placeholder + non-required pattern (v7) is gone:
  `disruption_type`, `delay_reason`, `stg_alternatives_sameday_sc`,
  `stg_alternatives_overnight_sc`, `stg_refund`, `stg_alternatives_sameday_td`,
  `stg_alternatives_overnight_td` are all `required: 1` with no placeholder option now, so
  Zingtree blocks Continue until the agent picks a real value - the "unanswered screen
  silently submits the first option" risk the old placeholder pattern was guarding against
  can no longer happen on any of them.
  CONDITIONAL FIELDS CAN BE REQUIRED SAFELY (confirmed by Brent 2026-08-24, correcting an
  assumption this file got wrong the same day): a `config.conditional` field's `required`
  constraint only enforces once the field actually renders (its condition is satisfied) - a
  required field that stays hidden does NOT block the node. So `delay_reason` (node 50 field
  1, node 66 field 1 - conditional on `disruption_type == "Trip delay"`) being `required: 1`
  is fine as-is; there was never a need to revert it, and an earlier pass this session did
  so incorrectly before Brent corrected it - it is back to `required: 1` here.
  `flight_affected` (node 50 field 2, node 66 field 2 - conditional on `disruption_type`
  containing "Schedule") stays `required: 0`, which is also fine either way given the above.
  The one dropdown that DID need a fix: Node 59's `stg_alternatives_overnight_sc` had its
  placeholder removed like the other ten but was left `required: 0` - the only one of the
  eleven not to get both changes together. Set to `required: 1` to match. Before that fix,
  an agent who clicked Continue on node 59 without touching the dropdown would have silently
  submitted its first option ("Alternative for the directly affected flight with hotel
  accomodation") as if they had offered it - node 60's first button matches that exact
  string and would have routed to 80 (offer accepted) on a screen the agent never actually
  answered, recording a false STG outcome.
- No persistent button. persist_names / persist_node_ids used to point at node 29 (Clear
  Data), which no longer exists in this tree; both are now empty. If you add one, point it
  at a node that exists.
- No persistent button. persist_names / persist_node_ids used to point at node 29 (Clear
  Data), which no longer exists in this tree; both are now empty. If you add one, point it
  at a node that exists.

## Open items
0. **Fixed here, but the same hole is still in the PARENT tree**: `bucketKey()` in the
   parent's nodes 2 and 46 dereferences `b.id` with no null guard, so a single Edvin action
   with a missing bucket throws and takes the whole node down. Node 81 here now returns ""
   for a null bucket (which node 27 then flags as bucket_missing, the correct outcome).
   Worth the one-line fix on the parent next time it is touched.
1. **The bare contact reason crashes node 81.** The parent's node 75 routes
   contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi (the parent value) into this tree, but
   CONTACT_REASON_BY_ZENDESK only maps the two leaf values (`_vi_sc`,
   `_vi_passengers_at_the_airport`), so that contact throws at node 81. The node now logs the
   Zendesk value, the resolved name and every category Edvin offered before throwing.
   Decide with ETG which leaf it means (or stop routing it) - do not guess a mapping.
2. **Node 12's action table still uses a `<style>` block, CSS classes and data-* attributes.**
   The parent tree removed all three at its v30 because the org's anti-injection sanitizer
   drops markup after a `<style>` block, which made the whole table - and every selection it
   captured - disappear. Left as-is by request. If the bucket still arrives blank, this is
   the first thing to check: node 27 now logs the raw value it read for each row.
3. **No unresolved-selection guard.** The parent halts a run it cannot resolve (its nodes
   50/51: re-pick, or escalate recording nothing). Here node 27 only flags and logs, so an
   unreadable selection still becomes a silent ticket. Porting the guard also needs a route
   away from the parent's node 44, which throws on an empty final_pnrs.
4. ~~**Passengers.**~~ **Done 2026-08-24.** Node 85 (Select Passengers - VI) / node 86
   (Continue) capture passengers via the same findorder Dynamic View the parent tree uses,
   and node 27 now carries `passengers`/`formatted_passengers` onto the child_ticket and
   final_pnrs records. See Data dictionary and the passenger bullet above.
5. **Node 1's `type` select still carries the 17 hardcoded Cancellation option labels and
   their `actions_array_name` scores** underneath the dynamic list source. They are dead
   weight for VI (the dynamic source wins) but they are what an agent sees if the dynamic
   list ever fails to load. Clear them or make them the VI type list.
6. **Node 48 (the old partner/orderCreated selection screen) is gone from this export, but
   node 82's comments and this file's changelog still describe it.** `partner` and
   `orderCreated` now have no agent-facing screen anywhere in this tree - node 82 reads them
   as already-set variables (an inbound query param, or a value the launching system seeds).
   Confirmed by grep: no formfield in this tree is named `partner` or `orderCreated`. Left
   as a documentation gap, not a functional bug - the CUTOFF COMPARE bullet above has been
   corrected, but confirm with Brent where these two values are actually meant to come from
   now, since node 82's own header comment (unedited) still says "Node 48 carries an
   orderCreated date field (the manual/testing entry)".

## Request status-check & selection guard (v13, 2026-08-25)

**Same pattern as the parent tree's v42 (see the parent's claude.md for the full
mechanism).** This tree only fires one direct API call - node 80 "Get Errand
Configurations" (CO 182 + 183) - so it gets one status-check pair: node 80's
continuation now points at new Scoring node 3 ("Get Errand Configurations -
Status Check"), which requires BOTH `actions.edvin__errand_configuration` and
`actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value` to report `_zt_meta.response.code` 200 or 201
before continuing to node 81 (Format Types, 80's original continuation,
unchanged); otherwise it routes to new Content node 4, "Get Errand
Configurations - Request Failed" (`zt-cb-type-alert`), with "Retry" -> back to
node 80 and "End Session::zt_request_failed" -> new node 6, "Session Ended -
Request Failed" (this tree's OWN terminal node - it does not jump back into the
parent tree; a request failure here ends the session directly rather than
returning through node 79).

**Passenger selection is validated the same way as the parent tree's node 9.**
Node 86 ("Continue") already had `views.findorder || []` (no bug to fix here,
unlike the parent's node 9); it now also sets a `has_passenger_selection`
form-data flag from that same array, and its continuation routes through new
Scoring node 7 ("Passenger Selection Made?") -> true: node 49 (86's original
continuation, unchanged) -> false: new Content node 8, "Please Make a Selection
- Passengers", whose "Try Again" button returns to node 85 (Select Passengers -
VI) to redo the grid selection. This tree does NOT get a PNR-selection guard -
per the existing Data dictionary entry above, PNR selection happens once in the
PARENT tree (its node 6/24) before this subtree is ever entered; this subtree
only reads `transforms.selected_pnrs` as an input, so re-validating it here would
be redundant and there is no PNR-selection screen in this tree to send an agent
back to.

New nodes this session: 3, 4 (status-check pair), 6 (error-end), 7, 8 (passenger
selection guard) - 5 total, filed under the lowest previously-unused node IDs.
No existing node was renumbered or deleted; only node 80's `continuation_node_id`
and node 86's script body were edited to redirect into the new guards.
